correctness.rationale: For any coloured a_i, with a coloured A-vertices and colour multiplicity u, the exact criterion is 2(u+epsilon_i)>=a+delta_i. Every A-colour has multiplicity >=ceil((a-1)/2). Hence a row supports at most three colours; three force exactly three differently coloured vertices and their matched partners of the same colours. This leaves at most three global colours. Four global colours therefore force two colours per row, disjoint palettes, equal positive row multiplicities, and no doubly-coloured matched edge; the converse holds with equality in every local majority. Direct enumeration of all partial set partitions for 1<=n<=5 and exact multinomial enumeration for optimizers are independently executable in verify.py. The proof, not finite experiments, establishes the infinite statements.

value.rationale: The theorem determines the exact parameter on an infinite dense regular family where both order and degree grow, with a sharp uniform ceiling four not supplied by the available general bound for n>=5. The structure theorem classifies all optimal maps, including balanced large same-colour classes, and gives an exact multinomial polynomial and Bessel-series exponential generating function for optimal named-palette assignments. This answers a natural structural and enumerative question for the recently studied invariant and is not a trivial small-bound instance or arbitrary parameter slice.
